alternatives.option: Define interfaces over every collection and connection type for mocking frameworks.
alternatives.whyRejected: Significantly widens the public API surface and complicates the nested generic object model across connections, shards, and shard sets.

alternatives.option: Require integration tests against live database instances.
alternatives.whyRejected: Slow and requires database infrastructure in every unit-test environment.

fields.consequences: Application data access code can be unit-tested through the production call path with canned results. The stored mock object must match the method's expected return type (for example, a `List<TModel>` for a `ReadAll` call), since mock short-circuiting bypasses the `Mapper`, ADO.NET command execution, and result handlers.
fields.context: Application data classes depend on concrete ArgentSea collection and connection singletons built from configuration. Without an in-memory short-circuit seam, unit-testing application data logic would require a live database or wrapper interfaces over every generic collection type.
fields.decision: Data connections, shards, and shard sets expose a `MockResults` dictionary keyed by `Query.Name`. When a data method is invoked with a `Query` whose name is present in `MockResults`, the stored object is returned immediately without opening a database connection, while parameter construction, method selection, and caller logic execute normally.
fields.title: Support unit testing by short-circuiting queries with mock results keyed by query name
